claims.text: Mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering can enable a large-scale in situ reaction between refractory alloying elements and Cu.
The proposed route forms a stable, refined Cu/refractory composite microstructure that limits adverse effects associated with positive heat of mixing.
The starting material is an unmixed, segmented powder blend of refractory elements and Cu.
High-energy mechanical alloying followed by SPS is a viable processing sequence for refractory-element powders.
This mechanical-alloying-plus-SPS sequence is applicable to a powder blend containing Cu and refractory elements.
SPS near 1400 °C under 30 MPa with a short dwell and rapid heating is an appropriate consolidation schedule.
An inert argon atmosphere is suitable for processing refractory alloys by powder-based rapid-consolidation methods.
A short SPS dwell restricts excessive diffusion between Cu and refractory elements.
SPS pressure promotes densification of the mechanically alloyed material.
SPS produces fine precipitates, interfacial phases, or a controlled intermetallic layer at Cu/refractory contacts.
Refined grain boundaries and interfacial phases act as barriers to uncontrolled Cu/refractory elemental mixing.
Rapid SPS consolidation minimizes diffusion time and detrimental Cu/refractory intermixing.
A short high-temperature pulse drives a controlled reaction that creates fine, stable interfacial phases.
The resulting interfacial phases stabilize the microstructure and preserve the designed composite architecture.
The SPS-processed Cu/refractory composite will have a fine, uniformly distributed microstructure with stable interfacial zones.
The SPS-processed composite will have greater mechanical strength and thermal stability than conventionally melted material.
Conventional melting or slow sintering causes excessive Cu/refractory diffusion and coarse, unstable microstructures with poor interfacial stability.
The proposed benefit depends on optimizing temperature, pressure, heating rate, and dwell time while avoiding prolonged high-temperature exposure.
The precise Cu/refractory interfacial chemistry under SPS conditions is uncertain.
The scalability of SPS for large nuclear-reactor components is uncertain.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis states that the route can enable a large-scale reaction, while the uncertainty field acknowledges that scalability to large components is unknown.
